title: Kuala Lumpur to Malacca EV Road Trip: A Short Family Adventure to Malaysia's Historic City
excerpt: Planning a family EV road trip from Kuala Lumpur to Malacca? This guide covers the best charging stations, costs, distances, and kid-friendly stops along the way. Discover how to make your journey smooth, affordable, and unforgettable.
author: EV Charging Asia Team
content:
## Introduction: Why a KL to Malacca EV Road Trip?

If you're looking for a short, family-friendly electric vehicle (EV) road trip in Malaysia, the drive from Kuala Lumpur to Malacca is hard to beat. The distance is just under 150 km, making it a perfect half-day journey even with stops for charging and sightseeing. Malacca, a UNESCO World Heritage city, offers a rich blend of history, culture, and delicious street food — and with the growing network of EV chargers along the North-South Expressway, the trip is now easier than ever for EV owners.

In this guide, we'll cover everything you need to know: the best charging stations, estimated costs, distances, family-friendly pit stops, and tips to keep your trip stress-free. Whether you drive a Tesla, BYD, or Hyundai Ioniq, this route is well-served. Let's plug in and go!

## Planning Your Route: KL to Malacca

The most direct route is via the North-South Expressway (E2), which takes about 1.5 to 2 hours without traffic. With an EV, you'll want to plan at least one charging stop, though many modern EVs can make the trip on a single charge. For safety and convenience, we recommend a top-up at a high-speed charger halfway.

### Key distances:
- Kuala Lumpur city center to Ayer Keroh toll plaza: ~140 km
- Ayer Keroh to Malacca city center: ~15 km
- Total driving distance: ~150 km

### Recommended charging stations along the route:

| Charging Station | Location | Distance from KL | Charger Type | Cost (per kWh) | Amenities |
|------------------|----------|------------------|--------------|----------------|-----------|
| Genting Sempah Shell Recharge | KM 34.3, E2 | 34 km | DC 50 kW | RM 1.20 | Shell café, restrooms, convenience store |
| Seremban R&R (Northbound) | KM 263, E2 | 65 km | DC 180 kW | RM 1.10 | Food court, surau, playground, petting zoo |
| Ayer Keroh R&R (Southbound) | KM 199, E2 | 140 km | DC 150 kW | RM 1.15 | Restoran, souvenir shops, rest area |
| Malacca City – Jaya 99 Charging Hub | Jalan Hang Tuah, Melaka | 150 km | AC 22 kW & DC 50 kW | RM 0.90 (AC) / RM 1.20 (DC) | Nearby cafes, parking, walking distance to Jonker Street |

*Note: Prices are approximate and may vary by operator. Always check the app for real-time rates.*

## Charging Costs: How Much Will You Spend?

Let's break down the cost for a typical family EV with a 60 kWh battery (e.g., BYD Atto 3 or Tesla Model 3 Standard Range). Assuming you start with 90% charge in KL and top up once at Seremban R&R:

- **Home charging (KL):** RM 0.218 per kWh (TNB tariff) – cost to charge 54 kWh (90%) = ~RM 11.77
- **Top-up at Seremban R&R (20 kWh):** 20 kWh x RM 1.10 = RM 22.00
- **Total charging cost for round trip (if you charge again in Malacca):** ~RM 50-60

Compared to a petrol car (RM 40-50 for the same distance), an EV is slightly cheaper, especially if you charge at home. Plus, many shopping malls in Malacca offer free or discounted charging for customers.

## Family-Friendly Stops and Tips

### 1. Seremban R&R (KM 263) – The Ultimate Pit Stop
This is a must-stop for families. The R&R has a large playground, a petting zoo with goats and rabbits, and clean restrooms. Let the kids burn off energy while you charge. Grab a bite at the food court — the nasi lemak and roti canai are excellent.

### 2. Ayer Keroh R&R – Last Charge Before Malacca
If you skipped Seremban, this is your final chance to charge before entering the city. The R&R has a small playground and souvenir shops. It's also the exit for the Ayer Keroh toll, so you can charge and then head straight to your hotel.

### 3. Malacca City Charging – Jaya 99 Hub
Located near Jonker Street, this hub has both AC and DC chargers. While charging, walk to the nearby cafes or let the kids enjoy the interactive museum at the same building. It's a great central spot.

### 4. Kid-Friendly Attractions in Malacca
- **Jonker Street Night Market** (weekends): Street food, toys, and live music.
- **Malacca River Cruise**: A relaxing boat ride that kids love.
- **The Shore Oceanarium**: Small but affordable aquarium with touch pools.
- **Taming Sari Tower**: Revolving observation deck for a bird's-eye view.

## Where to Stay in Malacca with EV Charging

Many hotels in Malacca now offer EV charging. Here are our top picks:

- **Hatten Hotel Melaka** (Jalan Melaka Raya): Has 2 Type 2 AC chargers. Centrally located near Dataran Pahlawan mall. Book your stay on Booking.com.
- **The Straits Hotel & Suites** (Jalan Malaka): Offers a dedicated EV parking bay with a 22 kW charger. Great for families with kids' pool and play area.
- **Casa del Rio Melaka** (Jalan Hang Tuah): Luxury option with valet charging. Perfect for a romantic getaway but also kid-friendly.

*Tip: Always call ahead to confirm charger availability, as some hotels require reservation.*

## What to Eat in Malacca (Family Edition)

No trip is complete without food. Here are family-approved spots:

- **Nancy's Kitchen** (Jalan Hang Jebat): Peranakan cuisine – try the chicken kapitan and cendol.
- **Bibik House Nyonya Cuisine** (Jalan Tun Tan Cheng Lock): Affordable and kid-friendly set meals.
- **Geographer Cafe** (Jalan Hang Jebat): Air-conditioned with a kids' menu and live music in the evenings.
- **Jonker 88** (Jalan Hang Jebat): Famous for its laksa and cendol – quick and casual.

## Must-Have Apps for Your EV Road Trip

- **PlugShare**: Find chargers, see reviews, and check availability.
- **ChargEV**: Covers most DC fast chargers along the highway.
- **JomCharge**: Good for AC chargers in Malacca city.
- **Waze**: Essential for traffic and finding chargers (many are listed).

## Sample Itinerary: 2 Days, 1 Night

### Day 1: KL to Malacca
- 9:00 AM: Depart KL with 90% charge.
- 9:45 AM: Stop at Seremban R&R for a 20-minute top-up and breakfast. Let kids play at the playground.
- 11:30 AM: Arrive in Malacca. Check into Hatten Hotel (park and plug in).
- 12:30 PM: Lunch at Nancy's Kitchen.
- 2:00 PM: Visit The Shore Oceanarium.
- 4:00 PM: Walk along Jonker Street (try cendol).
- 6:00 PM: Malacca River Cruise (book via Klook for discounts).
- 7:30 PM: Dinner at Geographer Cafe.
- 9:00 PM: Return to hotel. Charge overnight.

### Day 2: Explore and Return
- 8:00 AM: Breakfast at hotel.
- 9:30 AM: Visit Taming Sari Tower.
- 11:00 AM: Explore A Famosa and St. Paul's Church (free, easy walk).
- 12:30 PM: Lunch at Bibik House.
- 2:00 PM: Depart Malacca. Optional quick top-up at Ayer Keroh R&R if needed.
- 3:30 PM: Arrive KL. Charge at home or nearest station.

## Eco-Friendly Travel Tips for Families

- **Pre-cool your car while plugged in** to save battery on air conditioning.
- **Use regen braking** on the highway descents to recover energy.
- **Pack snacks and water** to avoid buying at overpriced R&R shops.
- **Bring a portable charger** as backup (some hotels have 13A sockets).
- **Teach kids about sustainability** – explain why you're driving an EV!

## Conclusion: A Smooth, Green Getaway

A Kuala Lumpur to Malacca EV road trip is not only feasible but also enjoyable for the whole family. With a growing network of fast chargers, affordable costs, and plenty of kid-friendly attractions, it's a perfect weekend escape. Whether you're a seasoned EV driver or new to electric travel, this route offers confidence and convenience. So pack your bags, charge up, and discover the historic charm of Malacca — the EV way.

*Have you done this trip? Share your experience in the comments below or tag us on social media. Safe travels!*
